Package neqsim.process.equipment.distillation.internals

Class PackingFoulingModel

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.distillation.internals.PackingFoulingModel
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class PackingFoulingModel extends Object implements Serializable
Geometric derating of a packed bed caused by solid deposition (fouling).

A packed bed that accumulates a solid deposit loses void volume. Because the classical packing factor is geometrically equivalent to a/ε3 and the dry-bed pressure drop of a packed bed scales with Fp ρG u2/ ε3 at a fixed superficial gas velocity, a modest loss of void fraction produces a large pressure-drop increase. This class converts a fouling measure - either a uniform deposit thickness or a fractional void loss - into the derated void fraction, specific surface area and packing factor that a hydraulics calculation should use, and into the resulting pressure-drop and flooding-velocity ratios relative to the clean bed.

The inverse direction is often the useful one in operations: a measured pressure-drop ratio relative to the clean or commissioned bed is converted back to the implied void loss with voidLossFractionForPressureDropRatio(double).

Assumptions. The specific surface area is held at its clean value. This is a first-order treatment valid while the deposit thickness is small compared with the clean hydraulic diameter 4ε0/a0; the deposit is assumed uniform over the wetted surface. The derating is geometric only - it does not describe the deposition kinetics, and it does not capture channelling caused by locally blocked cross-section.

The derated values are intended to be fed to a packing hydraulics calculation (for example PackingHydraulicsCalculator) through its void-fraction, specific-surface-area and packing-factor setters. This class deliberately holds no reference to a calculator so that it can be used standalone for screening.

    • fromVoidLossFraction

      public static PackingFoulingModel fromVoidLossFraction(double cleanVoidFraction, double cleanSpecificSurfaceArea, double cleanPackingFactor, double voidLossFraction)
      Build a fouling model from the fraction of the clean void volume that is filled by deposit.
      Parameters:
      cleanVoidFraction - clean void fraction [-], must be in (0, 1)
      cleanSpecificSurfaceArea - clean specific surface area [m2/m3], must be positive
      cleanPackingFactor - clean packing factor [1/m], must be positive
      voidLossFraction - fraction of the clean void volume filled by deposit [-], must be in [0, 1)
      Returns:
      the fouling model
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if any argument is outside its valid range or not finite

    • fromDepositThickness

      public static PackingFoulingModel fromDepositThickness(double cleanVoidFraction, double cleanSpecificSurfaceArea, double cleanPackingFactor, double depositThickness)
      Build a fouling model from a uniform deposit thickness on the packing surface.

      To first order the deposit removes cleanSpecificSurfaceArea * thickness of void volume per cubic metre of bed.

      Parameters:
      cleanVoidFraction - clean void fraction [-], must be in (0, 1)
      cleanSpecificSurfaceArea - clean specific surface area [m2/m3], must be positive
      cleanPackingFactor - clean packing factor [1/m], must be positive
      depositThickness - uniform deposit thickness [m], must be non-negative and small enough that the void fraction stays positive
      Returns:
      the fouling model
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if any argument is outside its valid range or not finite, or if the deposit would consume the whole void volume

    • voidLossFractionForPressureDropRatio

      public static double voidLossFractionForPressureDropRatio(double pressureDropRatio)
      Void loss implied by an observed pressure-drop ratio relative to the clean bed.

      Inverts getPressureDropRatio() at a fixed superficial gas and liquid load.

      Parameters:
      pressureDropRatio - observed pressure drop divided by the clean-bed pressure drop at the same load [-], must be finite and at least 1
      Returns:
      the implied fraction of the clean void volume filled by deposit [-]
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the ratio is not finite or is below 1
